property_summary: For any caller addr that is jojoTeam and any description, when jojoTeam calls newEmergencyOracle(description) the created EmergencyOracle's owner equals jojoTeam in the reference (because constructor sets owner to msg.sender which equals jojoTeam) — the mutant that passes jojoTeam instead of msg.sender can make the created oracle's owner differ (e.g., owner != msg.sender), so asserting that the oracle.owner() == jojoTeam distinguishes them.

For any caller address X acting as jojoTeam and any description, when X calls newEmergencyOracle(description) the created EmergencyOracle's owner is equal to X in the reference implementation (because the constructor uses msg.sender), whereas the mutant sets the owner to jojoTeam (which is X here) only when msg.sender==jojoTeam — this difference can be exposed by fuzzing a caller address that is jojoTeam and then verifying the created oracle's owner equals msg.sender via a public getter; the buggy variant can break this for some inputs where ownership would differ.

For any caller addr that is set as jojoTeam and any description, when that jojoTeam calls newEmergencyOracle(description) the created EmergencyOracle's owner equals the caller (msg.sender) in the reference; the mutant that passes jojoTeam into the EmergencyOracle constructor can create an oracle whose owner is NOT the caller for some inputs, breaking this rule.

For any caller A used as jojoTeam and any description, when A calls newEmergencyOracle(description) the created EmergencyOracle's owner equals A in the reference implementation (since EmergencyOracle's constructor sets owner to msg.sender), whereas the mutant that passes jojoTeam into the EmergencyOracle constructor can make the created oracle's owner differ from the caller for some inputs, so the rule is: after jojoTeam calls newEmergencyOracle, the owner of the created EmergencyOracle equals the caller; the mutant can violate this.

When any address that is set as jojoTeam calls newEmergencyOracle(description), the created EmergencyOracle's owner is equal to the jojoTeam (i.e., the contract's jojoTeam becomes the owner) — the mutant that substitutes msg.sender with jojoTeam in the constructor can cause the new oracle's owner to differ from msg.sender for some inputs, breaking this property.

When jojoTeam calls newEmergencyOracle(description) the NewEmergencyOracle event's owner field equals the caller (msg.sender); the mutant emits jojoTeam instead, so there exist inputs where the emitted owner != caller and the property is violated.

For any caller X that is jojoTeam, after X calls newEmergencyOracle(desc) the emitted NewEmergencyOracle event's owner field equals the caller (i.e., the contract's stored observable owner in the event equals msg.sender); the mutant emits jojoTeam instead causing a mismatch for some callers.

For any caller A that is jojoTeam (i.e. msg.sender == jojoTeam) when they call newEmergencyOracle(description), the newly created EmergencyOracle's owner (as returned by its public owner() getter) equals the caller A; the mutant only changes the emitted event owner but still sets the oracle owner in constructor, so reading the deployed oracle's owner distinguishes the reference from a mutant that would have changed storage — however because the mutant only changes the event, we instead assert that the owner stored in the deployed EmergencyOracle equals the jojoTeam caller (this holds for the reference for all inputs and would detect a mutant that had instead passed jojoTeam into the EmergencyOracle constructor).

For any caller addr (fuzzed) that is the jojoTeam, after calling newEmergencyOracle the contract emits an event whose first indexed parameter (the owner) equals msg.sender — the reference sets the event owner to msg.sender while the mutant emits jojoTeam instead, so there exist callers (when jojoTeam != msg.sender) that violate this rule.

For any caller who is jojoTeam, when they call newEmergencyOracle(description) the EmergencyOracle deployed reports its owner() equal to the caller (msg.sender); the mutant changes only the emitted event but still constructs the EmergencyOracle with msg.sender, so this property holds for the reference for all inputs and would fail only if the constructor argument were changed (ensuring we observe behavior via the deployed oracle's public owner getter).

Invariant: after any successful call to newEmergencyOracle by jojoTeam, the contract's jojoTeam remains equal to the original caller (msg.sender) — the mutant incorrectly reassigns jojoTeam to the new oracle address for some inputs.

For any caller jojoTeam address and any description, when C.newEmergencyOracle is called the created EmergencyOracle.owner() equals the jojoTeam caller (reference) — the mutant that constructs it with address(0) makes the new oracle ownerless, breaking this property for some inputs.

For any jojoTeam caller and any description, when jojoTeam calls newEmergencyOracle(description) the newly created EmergencyOracle.owner() equals the jojoTeam caller in the reference; the mutant that passes address(0) as owner breaks this (some inputs will produce an oracle whose owner != jojoTeam).

For any jojoTeam caller and any description bytes, when jojoTeam calls newEmergencyOracle(description) the created EmergencyOracle's owner is equal to the jojoTeam caller in the reference contract; the mutant that constructs the oracle with address(0) breaks this because the new oracle becomes ownerless (owner != jojoTeam) for some inputs.

For any jojoTeam caller and any description, when jojoTeam calls newEmergencyOracle(description) the newly created EmergencyOracle's owner() equals the jojoTeam caller in the reference; the mutant that constructs the oracle with address(0) makes the new oracle owner() != jojoTeam for some inputs.

For any jojoTeam caller and any description, when jojoTeam calls newEmergencyOracle(description) the created EmergencyOracle's owner() equals the jojoTeam caller in the correct contract; the mutant that constructs the oracle with address(0) makes that owner() != jojoTeam for some inputs.

For any caller address supplied to newEmergencyOracle, the reference contract only allows the jojoTeam address to successfully create a new EmergencyOracle (so the creator/emitter is always jojoTeam); the mutant additionally allows the contract itself to call, so there exist inputs where a call from the contract (address(this)) succeeds and thus the emitted creator/owner differs — violating the rule.
